title: Mock analysis sheet: marks by question
subject: English Language
unit: Summer 2: Timed Sections A and C; mock
source: Seeded from english-language/y10 lesson 68 (Mock analysis sheet: marks by question (pupil PDF))
intro: Mock paper. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: You have 35 minutes left and have not started Section C. Best move?
options: Plan for 3 minutes, write a shorter controlled piece, keep 3 minutes to check
Start a long, ambitious story with no plan
questions.a: B) Plan for 3 minutes, write a shorter controlled piece, keep 3 minutes to check. A short, controlled, accurate piece earns far more than a blank or an unfinished sprawl.

questions.q: Which target will lift a mid-level description most?
options: Add more adjectives to every noun
Build the piece around one sustained image
questions.a: C) Build the piece around one sustained image. A sustained image gives control and structure; extra adjectives or length do not.

questions.q: How should you choose your task?
options: the one I can plan fastest with a clear shape
questions.a: A) the one I can plan fastest with a clear shape. Speed of planning predicts control of the whole piece.

questions.q: Which corrects 'The crates thumped, the gulls cried.'?
options: The crates, thumped, the gulls cried.
The crates thumped; the gulls cried.
The crates thumped the gulls cried.
questions.a: B) The crates thumped; the gulls cried.. A semi-colon correctly joins two closely related clauses.

questions.q: Best answer to Q1?
options: about twenty or so, then rested a lot
questions.a: C) twenty. A precise one-word answer earns the mark; six hours is the length of the climb, not the steps.

questions.q: What most often holds Q7 back?
options: writing about one text, then the other, without comparing
questions.a: A) writing about one text, then the other, without comparing. Q7 rewards comparison in every paragraph, not two separate essays.

questions.q: build your personal timing plan for the paper, with start times written as clock times from 9:00
questions.a: A personal plan with clock times
questions.model: 9:00 read | 9:15 Section A | 10:15 Section B | 11:05 Section C | 11:55 check | 12:00 end

questions.q: write your recovery rules for overrunning in each section
explain why Q7 deserves more time than Q3, using marks
questions.a: Q7 is worth 15 marks against 10, so about a third more time

questions.q: Fill the timing plan: sections and minutes adding to 180
rewrite the first two paragraphs of your Spring 2 piece, applying your targets
questions.model: Before: 'It was snowing on the road. It was very cold.' | After: 'The snow came in the night, quietly, as if it did not want to wake anyone.' (sustained image begins)

questions.q: write your five-line plan for tomorrow's full timed rewrite
list three AO5 upgrades you will use (a colon, a short sentence, a precise verb)
Write your two AO4 targets and one AO5 target
questions.a: For example: AO4: sustain one image; control the ending. AO5: no comma splices.
questions.model: I do: I read the teacher's comments and the ladder, then write targets as actions: 'Sustain one image from start to end.'

questions.q: write your piece in the portal response box
questions.a: Marked with the 4EB1 Section C criteria: AO4 20, AO5 10
questions.model: No model during the timed piece; peers and the teacher mark next lesson.

questions.q: edit and proofread (3 minutes) using your error log
underline where you applied each target
Plan (5 minutes): five lines, with your targets written at the top
questions.model: Teacher reminder only: targets at the top; wide, lens, movement, sound, return.

questions.q: peer-mark a classmate's piece in a breakout room: levels, evidence, one target
questions.model: AO4 level + quotation | AO5 level + quotation | One target

questions.q: act on your own target: polish three sentences
rewrite your ending to echo your opening
Place the model extract on the AO5 ladder with one quotation
questions.a: Middle, with a comma splice as evidence
questions.model: I do: I find two comma splices and some varied vocabulary: middle level.

questions.q: questions 1 to 6
questions.a: Marked with the mark scheme: Q1 twenty; Q2 cloud; Q3 and Q6 to the 10-mark levels; Q4 four o'clock; Q5 two of: few words, few teeth, led by lantern
questions.model: No model during the timed answers. Keep to the plan: Q1, Q2 one minute each; Q3 10 minutes; Q4, Q5 three minutes; Q6 10 minutes (shortened to fit the lesson).

questions.q: note your Q7 plan: two similarities and two differences in the writers' perspectives
check every short answer is precise
Read both texts (5 minutes) and annotate for Q3 and Q6
questions.model: Teacher reminder: read Text One for Q3, Text Two for Q6; note two Q7 links as you go.

questions.q: DIRT: rewrite one Q7 paragraph so it compares in every sentence
questions.model: Before: 'Text One is about a climb. Text Two is also about a climb.' | After: 'Both writers find the summit unexpected, but whereas...'

questions.q: improve your weaker 10-mark answer (Q3 or Q6) using the model
write two Section A targets for the mock
questions.a: For example: compare in every Q7 sentence; explain one effect per quotation

questions.q: Write a comparative sentence using 'whereas' about the two writers' feelings
questions.a: For example: Whereas the first writer laughs, the second weeps.
questions.model: I do: Text One feeling + whereas + Text Two feeling.

questions.q: check short answers are precise
add one more Section B idea to your notes
Read both texts (6 minutes): annotate for Q3, Q6 and Q7, and note two Section B ideas from each
questions.a: Annotated texts and four Section B ideas
questions.model: Teacher reminder only: Section B ideas: kindness (Mr Osei's tomatoes; the flower-girl), community, a daily routine.

questions.q: write your article in the portal response box. Starter: a headline, then your opening
questions.a: Marked with the Q8 criteria: ideas from both texts transformed (AO1); article form and register for newspaper readers (AO4); accurate, varied writing (AO5)
questions.model: No model during the mock; shared in feedback: 'Why Our Market Matters. At five in the morning, while most of the town sleeps, a village wakes up...'

questions.q: proofread (3 minutes)
check you covered all three bullets
Plan (5 minutes): six ideas, three from each text, in your own words, under the three bullets
questions.model: Teacher reminder only: kindness (Osei, the flower-girl), community ('a village'), fairness to the poor (bruised fruit), daily routine.

questions.q: proofread (3 minutes) with your error log
improve your final sentence
Choose and plan (6 minutes): five lines
questions.model: Teacher reminder only: choose the task you can plan fastest; keep a story small; sustain one image.

questions.q: DIRT: rewrite your weakest Section A answer using the model
questions.a: An improved answer in a different colour
questions.model: Before: 'The writer uses lots of description of the market.' | After: 'The structure moves from plenty to the poor at "the closing hour"...'

questions.q: correct your Q5 so it gives two distinct points
write a sentence explaining the irony of 'the richest person in the place'
